before.exam_tip_html: In the writing and speaking exams, the examiner is looking for a range of vocabulary and tenses. When describing hobbies, don’t just list activities — give opinions, reasons, and show you can use gern / lieber / am liebsten to compare preferences. Using weil clauses with correct word order demonstrates grammatical accuracy and pushes your mark into the higher bands.

In the writing exam, the mark scheme rewards students who use multiple time frames successfully. When writing about sport, include present tense (what you do now), perfect tense (what you did recently), and future or conditional tense (what you will or would like to do). Getting the haben vs sein distinction right in the perfect tense is a common way to show grammatical accuracy.

In AQA reading and listening papers, personality adjectives appear constantly. Learn them in pairs (freundlich/unfreundlich, geduldig/ungeduldig, höflich/unhöflich) so you can quickly identify both positive and negative descriptions. In writing tasks, examiners reward students who give balanced descriptions — say something positive and something negative about the person.

In the Foundation writing paper, the 50-word response about food often asks you to mention foods you like, dislike, and a restaurant visit. Always use gern/nicht gern/lieber/am liebsten after the verb, justify your opinion with weil (because), and include at least one conditional phrase (ich möchte) to show range. Listing only vocabulary without forming sentences will not score well — the examiner wants to see you use the words in context.
